title: Special relativity basics
examples: What does the speed of light mean in special relativity?
How does time dilation affect moving objects?
Can you explain the basic postulates of special relativity?

explain.say: Today we learn about special relativity basics. First we look at the postulates of special relativity.

items: The laws of physics are the same for all non-accelerating observers.
The speed of light in vacuum is constant for all observers.

explain.say: The first postulate says physics laws are constant for everyone. For example, an experiment on Earth works the same way on a fast train.

draw.text: Physics laws constant for all inertial frames

explain.say: The second postulate is very important too. It states the speed of light is always constant. This is c, the speed of light.
Now we look at time dilation. This means time passes differently for different observers. The faster something moves, the slower time passes for it.

draw.text: Time passes slower when moving fast

explain.say: The formula for time dilation is delta t equals gamma times delta t naught. Here delta t naught is the time at rest.
For a real life example consider GPS satellites. They move fast, so their clocks run slightly slower than clocks on Earth.

faq.q: Does time dilation only happen at very high speeds?
faq.a: Time dilation effects become noticeable only when speeds approach the speed of light. At everyday speeds, the difference is too small to measure.
asks: Is time slowing down a real thing?

faq.q: What is the difference between proper time and dilated time?
faq.a: Proper time is the time measured by a clock at rest relative to the events. Dilated time is the time measured by an observer watching the moving clock.
asks: Which time measurement is the 'real' one?
What is the time measured by the person on the clock?

faq.q: Does this mean that everyone sees time differently?
faq.a: Yes, according to special relativity, the measurement of time intervals depends on the relative motion between the observers. This is a core concept of the theory.

faq.q: Why do we not notice time dilation in our daily lives?
faq.a: Because the speeds we experience daily are extremely small compared to the speed of light. The effects are negligible at low velocities.
asks: Why is it so hard to measure this?
Is it only an effect for astronauts?

faq.q: What does the Lorentz factor gamma represent?
faq.a: The Lorentz factor, gamma, is a factor that depends on the relative speed. It mathematically accounts for the time stretching effect.
asks: What is the formula for gamma?
How is gamma related to speed?

facts: The postulates apply to all inertial reference frames.
The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 300,000 kilometers per second.
Time dilation predicts that moving clocks run slower relative to a stationary observer.
The effect becomes significant only at speeds approaching the speed of light.

quiz.say: If a spaceship travels at a very high speed, how will a clock on Earth appear to a person on the ship?
quiz.why: Because the observer on the ship sees Earth time dilated, meaning it runs slower.

wrong.2: This reverses the direction of the time dilation effect.
wrong.3: Time only appears stopped at infinite speed, not just very high speeds.
